diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is well known that the eigenvalues of the palindromic matrix polynomial $P(\lambda)$ always occur in pairs $(\lambda, 1/\lambda^{\star})$

issues.failure_explanation: For $\star = H$ the palindromic pairing is $(\lambda, 1/\bar\lambda)$, which collapses to a single eigenvalue on the unit circle ($1/\bar\lambda = \lambda$), so unimodular eigenvalues of $H$-palindromic/$H$-anti-palindromic polynomials are not forced to occur with identical Jordan blocks twice. Yet Case 2 writes every unimodular block doubled, $J_j=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_jI+N,\lambda_jI+N)$, forcing even algebraic multiplicity at each unimodular eigenvalue (dimension count $2(n_1+\cdots+n_r)=2n$). Counterexamples: $P(\lambda)=\lambda^2+1$ ($A=1,Q=0,\epsilon=1$) is $H$-palindromic with two simple unimodular eigenvalues $\pm i$; $P(\lambda)=\lambda^2+2\lambda+1$ has a single Jordan block of size 2 at $-1$. Neither fits the claimed structure, contradicting also the paper's own introduction, which only asserts pairing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the duplicated unimodular block by a single block $J_j=\lambda_jI_{n_j}+N_{n_j}$ and characterize the corresponding parameter block directly as $\Gamma_{jj}\in\mathcal{S}_{(J_j,H,\epsilon)}$, i.e. $S_j\in\Theta_{(\lambda_j,\bar\lambda_j,j)}$ with $S_j^H=-\epsilon S_j$; restate thm-gamma-2 (single $n_j\times n_j$ unimodular blocks), the $H$-part of cor-1 ($1\times1$ blocks $\psi\in {\rm i}\mathbb{R}$ resp. $\mathbb{R}$ for simple unimodular eigenvalues), and harmonize thm-s-2; the paper's Stein/Sylvester arguments apply to single blocks unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: For the two $H$-classes, the advertised general characterization of the parameter matrix (Theorem thm-gamma-2, with its $2\times2$ unimodular blocks in (gs-38)), the semi-simple normalization (Theorem thm-s-2) and the simple-spectrum form in Corollary cor-1 cover only polynomials whose unimodular eigenvalues have evenly duplicated Jordan structure; general $H$-palindromic polynomials with unimodular eigenvalues (e.g., any simple unimodular eigenvalue) fall outside the theory, and the $H$-case IEP/EEP applications inherit this restriction.
issues.title: H-palindromic unimodular eigenstructure is wrongly forced into identical Jordan-block pairs
issues.why_classification: The error excludes a generic regime for the $H$-classes, but the repair reuses the paper's own machinery (the off-diagonal Sylvester-nonsingularity analysis is unchanged, and the single-block unimodular computation already appears in the proof of thm-s-2), so a contained re-derivation restores a comparable characterization without new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: For $i\neq k$ the block of $Z\in\Theta_{(a,b,j)}$ satisfies $aZ_{ik}N_k^T+bN_iZ_{ik}+N_iZ_{ik}N_k^T=0$; direct expansion (e.g., for the $3\times2$ block in Example exa1) forces exactly the entries with $s+t\ge\min\{n_i^{(j)},n_k^{(j)}\}+2$ to vanish, leaving the $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$ entries of a $3\times2$ block free — exactly as Example exa1 displays ($f_{12}, f_{21}$ free). The stated rule $s+t\ge\max\{n_i^{(j)},n_k^{(j)}\}$ ($=3$ in the example) would force $f_{12}=f_{21}=0$, contradicting both the computation and the paper's own example; even for two equal-size off-diagonal blocks the rule is wrong ($\max=n$ instead of the correct $n+2$).

failure_location.quote: $Z_{ik}\in\mathbb{C}^{n_i^{(j)}\times n_k^{(j)}}$ is a matrix that the $(s,t)$-element of $Z_{ik}$ is zero if $s+t\geq\max\{n_i^{(j)}, n_k^{(j)}\}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the off-diagonal rule by "the $(s,t)$-entry of $Z_{ik}$ is zero if $s+t\ge\min\{n_i^{(j)},n_k^{(j)}\}+2$", matching Example exa1 and the direct expansion.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit structural description of the solution set $\Theta_{(a,b,j)}$ is wrong for off-diagonal Jordan sub-blocks (it over-restricts the free entries), misleading any explicit parameter construction based on (gs-28); the set $\Theta_{(a,b,j)}$ itself, defined by the equation (gs-19) and used in thm-gamma and thm-gamma-2, is unaffected.
issues.title: Off-diagonal zero-pattern rule for $\Theta_{(a,b,j)}$ in (gs-28) is wrong and contradicts Example exa1
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the pattern rule restores consistency with the paper's own example; all theorem statements reference the equation-defined set $\Theta_{(a,b,j)}$, so no substantive claim or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: With the SVD $W_1=UD\overline V^T=UDV^H$ and $P=\mathrm{diag}(U,\overline V)$, the (1,2)-block of $PWP^T$ is $UW_1(P^T)_{22}=UW_1V^H=U^2D(V^H)^2$, which need not equal $D$: for $n=1$, $W_1=e^{{\rm i}\theta}$ ($U=e^{{\rm i}\theta}$, $V=1$) gives $PWP^T=\begin{bmatrix}0 & e^{2{\rm i}\theta}\\ -\epsilon e^{2{\rm i}\theta} & 0\end{bmatrix}\neq\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\ -\epsilon & 0\end{bmatrix}$ whenever $\theta\notin\pi\mathbb{Z}$. The verification asserted in the proof is false as written; the correct choice is $P=\mathrm{diag}(U^{-1},\overline V^{-1})=\mathrm{diag}(U^H,V^T)$, for which the (1,2)-block becomes $U^HW_1V=D$ and (gs-30) holds.

failure_location.quote: Denote by $P=\mbox{diag}(U, \overline{V})$. It is easy to verify that (\ref{gs-30}) holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $P=\mbox{diag}(U,\overline V)$ by $P=\mbox{diag}(U^{-1},\overline V^{-1})$ (still unitary since $U,V$ are unitary); the rest of the proof and all downstream uses are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The constructive step of Lemma lem-3's proof is wrong, so the normalization quoted again inside the proof of Theorem thm-s-1 cannot be used as written; the statements of lem-3 and thm-s-1 themselves remain valid once the corrected congruence is used.
issues.title: Lemma lem-3's explicit unitary $P=\mathrm{diag}(U,\overline V)$ does not achieve the claimed canonical form (gs-30)
issues.why_classification: The lemma's statement is true and the correction is a single forced change to the displayed congruence; no downstream claim, construction, or guarantee needs modification.

issues.failure_explanation: The only available justification is Theorem main-thm (thm-IEP is given no proof), whose sufficiency part requires $\Gamma\in\mathcal{S}_{(\Lambda,\star,\epsilon)}$, i.e. $\Lambda\Gamma=\Gamma\Lambda^{-T}$ for the complex diagonal $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{2n})$. Corollary cor-1's $T$-case forms are built for the real Jordan form $J_R=M\Lambda M^{-1}$; against the complex diagonal $\Lambda$, the intertwining for a quadruple block $\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_j,\bar\lambda_j,\lambda_j^{-1},\bar\lambda_j^{-1})$ forces the off-diagonal block $U_j$ to commute with $\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_j,\bar\lambda_j)$, i.e. to be diagonal, so a general block $U_j=\begin{bmatrix}a_j&b_j\\b_j&-a_j\end{bmatrix}$ with $b_j\neq0$ satisfies the stated hypotheses but not main-thm's, and the conclusion fails: with $n=2$, $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(2i,-2i,-i/2,i/2)$, $X=[e_1,e_2,e_1,e_2]$ and $U=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$, one gets $X\Gamma X^T=0$ and $X\Lambda\Gamma X^T=\frac{5i}{2}\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}$ nonsingular, but the formulas give $A=\frac{2i}{5}\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}$, $Q=-\frac35\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$ with $P(2i)e_1=\frac{4i}{5}e_2\neq0$: the prescribed eigenpairs are not recovered.

given by Corollary \ref{cor-1} such that $X\Gamma X^{\star}=0$ and $X\Lambda\Gamma X^{\star}$ is nonsingular.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to "$\Gamma\in\mathcal{S}_{(\Lambda,\star,\epsilon)}$ is nonsingular, $X\Gamma X^\star=0$ and $X\Lambda\Gamma X^\star$ is nonsingular" — for the $T$-cases this means using the blocks of Theorem thm-gamma associated with the complex diagonal $\Lambda$ (equivalently restricting cor-1's $U_j$ to be diagonal), or first passing to the real standard pair $(X_R,J_R)$; Theorem main-thm then yields the conclusion directly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated sufficient condition for solvability of the PQIEP is unreliable for the $T$-palindromic/$T$-anti-palindromic cases whenever the free blocks $U_j$ are not diagonal: the formulas can then produce a polynomial having the prescribed eigenvalues but not the prescribed eigenvectors. (The simplified construction following the theorem uses the diagonal choice $U=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$ and is not affected.)
issues.title: Theorem thm-IEP's sufficient condition is insufficient for the $T$-cases: Corollary cor-1's $\Gamma_R$ need not lie in $\mathcal{S}_{(\Lambda,\star,\epsilon)}$ for the complex diagonal $\Lambda$
issues.why_classification: The theorem as stated is false for admissible data (explicit counterexample) and no proof is given; the repair restricts the admissible parameter family to the intertwining-compatible forms — a limited weakening that keeps the same formulas and the same application but changes the stated solvability condition, so it exceeds a local fix while requiring no new proof architecture.

issues.title: Theorem thm-eep omits the nonsingularity of the updated collocation matrix that its proof and its formulas require
issues.why_classification: The theorem's universal guarantee is false as stated (the formulas can be undefined for admissible inputs), so the quantifier must be restricted by an additional, non-automatic nonsingularity condition — a limited weakening that leaves the method, the formulas, and the no-spill-over guarantee intact for all nondegenerate choices, with no new proof architecture.
